Welcome aboard

Setup wizard

Where should the logbook live?

The logbook is a single file, saved on your ship's network drive (NAS) so everyone in the engine room can open and edit it.

You have entries from this session that have not been saved yet. Create a new log file to keep them, or open an existing log file to switch to its saved data instead (this will replace what you entered here).

Install app & shortcuts

Your log file is connected. For quick access next time, you can install this as its own app and pin it to the desktop.

Step 1

Install the app

Installing also means it reconnects to your log file automatically every time - opened as a plain browser tab, it only remembers permission until you close the tab, then needs one click to reconnect.

Already installedThis is running as its own app right now, not a browser tab.
This page was opened directly from a file, which browsers won't let install as an app or work offline. It needs to be reachable at an http:///https:// address first (even http://localhost counts) - ask whoever set this file up how it's normally opened, or see the setup notes that came with it.

Your browser can install this with one click.

Your browser doesn't offer a one-click install here, but this only takes a moment by hand:

  1. Click the install icon (a small monitor with a ↓, or a ⊕) at the right end of the address bar - or the ⋮ menu → Cast, save and share → Install page as app.
  2. Confirm the name and click Install.
  1. Click the app icon at the right end of the address bar - or the ... menu → Apps → Install this site as an app.
  2. Confirm the name and click Install.
  1. Open the File menu → Add to Dock… (Safari 17+ / macOS Sonoma or newer).
  2. Confirm the name and click Add - it now opens as its own app from the Dock.
  3. On older Safari versions this option isn't available - use the bookmark step below instead.
  1. Tap the Share icon (a square with an arrow pointing up).
  2. Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen.
  3. Confirm the name and tap Add - this also takes care of Step 2 below, the icon lands straight on your Home Screen.
  1. Firefox doesn't currently support installing sites as standalone apps.
  2. Use the bookmark step below (Step 3), or open this page in Chrome or Edge for the full installed-app experience.

Step 2

Add a desktop shortcut

Once it's installed (Step 1), give it an icon on your desktop too:

  1. Go to chrome://apps (Chrome) or edge://apps (Edge) in the address bar.
  2. Right-click the Engineroom Log icon → Create shortcuts…
  3. Tick Desktop (and Start menu / taskbar if you'd like those too) and click Create.
  1. Installed apps show up in Launchpad and in your Applications folder automatically.
  2. To put an icon on the Desktop too: open Applications in Finder, find Engineroom Log, then right-click it and choose Make Alias - drag that alias onto the Desktop.

On a phone or tablet, Step 1 already puts the icon on your Home Screen - there's no separate desktop step there.

Step 3

Pin it in your browser

Prefer opening it as a regular tab sometimes? Bookmark it so it's one click away - browsers don't let a page bookmark itself automatically, so this one's manual:

then press Ctrl+D (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+D (Mac) to bookmark it

Once installed (Step 1), it also shows up on its own in chrome://apps / edge://apps - no bookmark needed to find it there.

You can skip this and set it up later - the logbook works the same either way.

                    Welcome aboard

                    Would you like to open a short quick start guide to this application?

                    Quick start guide

                    Logbook, ROB and UMS

                    The three main columns record engine room activity. Logbook is for watch remarks, ROB (remaining on board) tracks FO, LO and FW stock, and UMS records unmanned machinery space periods. Fill in the fields and press Save. Use Show all below each panel to view the full history.

                    ROB Tank levels

                    Press the report icon above ROB to open ROB Tank levels and enter each tank's reading. From there, open the Bridge/Locopias report to see all tanks on the ship's plan and confirm the readings.

                    Settings

                    Open Settings (gear icon, top right) to switch between light, dark and system appearance, see or change the connected shared log file, or download a backup copy of all data. You can reopen this guide from Settings at any time. Have a question that isn't answered here? Settings → Contact details lets you send it directly.

                    Reminder

                    Restore unsaved changes?

                    A change from a previous session in this browser never made it into - it was on screen but not yet saved when the file changed underneath it.

                    Restoring replaces everything currently loaded with that unsaved version, so only use it if you're sure nothing newer (saved by anyone since) needs to be kept. When in doubt, discard it and re-enter the change by hand instead.

                    Shared file updated by someone else

                    Another user saved changes to since you loaded it. Your most recent change here was not saved, to avoid overwriting theirs.

                    Click Reload to pick up the latest data, then re-enter your last change. It's also been kept in this browser and offered back to you as a restorable backup once you're reconnected.
